segments.he: בפעם האחרון שר"א ז"ל הי' באומין ואז התחיל המלחמה והי' עושה כל מיני עצות לגנוב הגבול כדי לבא לא"י והי' מתמרמר מאד על ציון הק' והי' צועק רבי אתם בעל כח שיכולים לשכב בחו"ל אבל אני צריך לשכב בא"י והי' מתמרמר מאד על הזמן השנה זו תרצו בגימ' צרות רח"ל וביקש תמיד על כלל ישראל וכמעט כל תפלתו הי' על הכלל והי' צועק כמה דמים נשפכו הלא הם אינם החפשים אשמים כ"כ כי הם תינוק שנשבה ורחמיו על כל מעשיו יתמו חטאים ולא חוטאים וכו' וכן הי' מאד מלמד זכות על כל ישראל ששם ישראל נקרא עליו.
segments.en: In Breslov there was a cantor whom the townspeople suspected [of wrongdoing], G-d preserve us. When he saw that Rabbainu had been chosen as Admor in his town, he began to shelter himself near Rabbainu. On the first Shabbos that Rabbainu entered Breslov, all the townspeople were there — and throughout that Shabbos, at almost every meal, this cantor requested Rabbainu's permission to sing a melody. But Rabbainu declined. And Rabbainu said the Torah of chapter 3, which speaks of melody and the one who hears melody from a wicked musician — how difficult this is for his service of G-d. And the townspeople understood that Rabbainu knew through his holy spirit about that cantor's sin. Only on motzei Shabbos, when the man pressed himself greatly to sing, Rabbainu said to him: "Now sing Hamavdil." He began to sing — and instead of the word "chalfa onas minchasi" [the time of my offering has passed] as written in the melody, he sang: "chalfa onas mitati" [the time of my bed has passed — alluding to his sin]. Everyone said: "Listen to what he testifies about himself!" And a great laughter arose, and he was greatly shamed — and from shame and anger he went and converted [to Christianity].
